rv: I'm not sure what the previous reviewers were thinking. Yes, this film is graphic, but not disgusting by any means. The film is rather dated (1937), but overall I'd say it gives a good non-politically corrected presentation of mammalian reproduction and birth.

Another one of these films that look far too innocent in the beginning, but then turn on you and gets graphic. The initial stages of this shows plenty of mammals and their young, like deer.. and rabbits.. Wait a minute! Did we see say Rabbit? Ever wonder how a rabbit is born? Why, we'll show you! Then it cuts into (literally) a rabbit being dissected and we see it's ovaries. Geez. After that, a pretty detailed course on how a rabbit egg is fertilized and grows. At the very end, I am not making this up, we cut into another rabbit, to see the rabbits ovaries with rabbit young still inside! then…

Developi1951: Social guidance film showing how necessary self-reliance is to all successful endeavors and happiness.

rv: Oh MAN! The return of ALAN WOODRUFF!!!

In this otherwise unegaging claptrap of becoming more self reliant, the whole thing is eclipsed over the return of three of the characters of one of my favorite movies on this site, 'Dating: Do's and Don'ts[' Alan Woodruff, his Mom and Dad, and there's even reference to his girlfriend Ann. Although Alan's last name is not mentioned, it's perfectly clear that it's him, with his parents and all. Anyways, Alan is clearly grown up in this picture, and this time he is fighting self reliance. He turns to his teacher (his French teacher?) who of course, gives him a chart about how to become more…
A good 1951 teenage guidance film about being self- reliant. Well written, acted, & directed. Many points are still good today.

This Coronet film stars Woody from Dating Dos and Donts, though its not nearly as campy as the other film. Now that hes got dating under control, his next problem is being to dependent on others, so a teacher gives him a set of simple steps to self-reliance, and soon Woody is so self-reliant hes taking over whole projects at the Student Council. Of course, the adults responsible for this film didnt really want teens to make their own decisions, or rather, they only wanted them to make their own decisions of their decisions were ones the adults would have made for them. Still, this film is not…

Assume responsibility? What the heck is that? Someone's mother, in 1950, knows about "Self Reliance" by Ralph Waldo Emerson? Not in my 1950 world. It was "Movie Mirror" and "Tattler" - and those were the literate ones. Alan still has the big fat dad that looks like Jackie Gleason's Bowery twin. Hated Ralph Waldo and wasn't too impressed with this film. Too sober a topic and a little lean on good ol camp.

rv: Great movie. Sterling Heyden plays an Army engineer for the new Kansas Pacific RR pre-Civil War. Lots of action, good story. Well worth the watch.

1. They showed the Capital dome, that was not done until 1863. 2. The use of weapons is advanced; by using a repeating rifles and 45 Colt. These did not come into being until the mid 1860's. 3. The film is supposed to be in Cinecolor and yet here it is in B/W.

rv: Man Against Crime ran on CBS from October 7, 1949, until October 1953. DuMont had it from October 1953 through April 1954. It was also simulcast on NBC from October 1954 through its DuMont run, and continued on NBC until July 1954. It returned to NBC in July and August 1956, as a live program with Frank Lovejoy replacing Ralph Bellamy. Follow That Man was the syndication title for the show. This information is from "The Complete Directory to Prime Time Network TV Shows."

rv: Ida Lupino is one of my all time favorite performers, and she does.a creditable job in this one. Too bad the other 2 actors turned out to be complete nobodies.

Ida Lupino is a rich lady who dumps her handsome younger husband (Scott Forbes) and moves to NYC to sublet a penthouse suite for a few months. Within just an hour, she is begging to leave. Very creepy story, which would have been better if Lupino hadn't overacted her fear.

rv: Very cute cartoon/advertisement which tells of a 'boy' (???) who falls in love witha girl (??) and rescues her from the clutches of a bad guy. The reason I put the boy and girl in quotes is because from the looks of the cartoon, they don't look to be pushing 12, so it's very alarming to see the girl doing Mae West moves and the huge bad guy making the moves on her. Oh yeah, since this is a Jem Handy pic, a very convenient chevrolet rams through the castle (with no damage) and saves the day. Truly a fairy tale.

Silly toon in typical 1930's style with catchy music and Middle Ages adventure theme. Starts out meandering, but soon we are in a great battle in which a boy with a wooden sword ends up defeating the bad knight by unleashing an awesome weapon: A Chevy! The power of many horses, moving fortress, great speed! It can drive through the castle wall! That's what Jam Handy is all about!
